title: Measure to the nearest whole unit

beats.say: The eraser starts at zero and ends on five. How long is it?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The eraser starts at $0$ and ends at $5$ cm. How long is it?

beats.say: Each space from one number to the next is a unit.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: One equal space used to measure.

beats.say: Cm means centimeters. A centimeter is this ruler's unit.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three, four, five.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: That count is the length, from one end to the other.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Length: how many units from end to end.

beats.say: It starts at zero, so the end number is the length.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Five centimeters.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The end number matches because the eraser starts at zero.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: And the end lands on a numbered mark.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Measure the block to the nearest centimeter. How long is it?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Measure the block to the nearest centimeter. How long is it?

beats.say: What does nearest mean?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Nearest means the numbered mark closer to the end.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: The numbered mark closer to the end.

beats.say: Five full spaces fit, so I say five.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Five full spaces do fit.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The end sits between five and six.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: What is the short mark with no number?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: That short mark is halfway between five and six.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Halfway: the short mark between the numbers.

beats.say: Each side of it is the same distance.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The end is past the halfway mark.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Line up how far the end is from five and from six.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How far it is from six is shorter.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Six is closer, so the block is about six centimeters.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: About six means six is the closest whole centimeter.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The strip starts at zero and ends between five and six. How long is it?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The strip starts at $0$ and ends between $5$ and $6$. How long is it?

beats.say: It is between the numbers. Does between always mean the bigger one?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Look at the halfway mark. The end has not reached it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Line up how far the end is from five and from six.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How far it is from five is shorter this time.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five is closer. The strip is about five centimeters.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Not yet at halfway: choose the smaller number.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Past halfway: choose the bigger number.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Not yet: the smaller number. Past: the bigger number.

beats.say: The same eraser is back at zero.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: It slides along the ruler.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Measure the eraser to the nearest centimeter. How long is it?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Measure the eraser to the nearest centimeter. How long is it?

beats.say: It ends at seven, so it is seven centimeters.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The filled spaces slid with it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three, four, five. Still five spaces.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: If I count the marks from two to seven, I get six.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The marks are the edges of the spaces.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two empty spaces sit before the eraser.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Seven counts from zero, so it includes them.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Seven minus two is five.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five centimeters.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The end is on a mark, so this length is exact.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Count the spaces from the start mark.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Count the spaces from the start mark. The number at the end counts from zero.

beats.say: The number at the end counts from zero.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Measure the ribbon to the nearest inch. How long is it?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Measure the ribbon to the nearest inch. How long is it?

beats.say: The ruler says in. Is an inch a unit too?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: An inch is one space on this ruler.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The ribbon starts at one, not at zero.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The end is between three and four, past the halfway mark.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Line up how far the end is from three and from four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How far it is from four is shorter, so four is closer.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Count the spaces from one to four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four minus one is three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The ribbon is about three inches.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Measure the block to the nearest centimeter. How long is it?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Measure the block to the nearest centimeter. How long is it?

beats.say: Where does the block start?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: It starts at four, not at zero.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The end is between ten and eleven.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Which mark is nearer to the end?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The end has not reached the halfway mark.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Line up the two distances.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How far it is from ten is shorter. Ten is closer.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Count the spaces from four to ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three, four, five, six.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Ten minus four is six.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Four plus six lands on ten.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The block is about six centimeters.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: I find the closer mark, then count from the start.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The centimeter lengths can stand on a line.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One length on five.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Another length on five. They stack.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One length on six.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Another length on six.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: On a line plot, each X is one length.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: A line plot: each X is one length.

beats.say: Two X's on five means two lengths of five, not a length of two.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The short mark only chose the numbered mark under the X.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Later, a ruler can let that short mark name a length.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Later, the short mark can name a length.

beats.say: Every length on a ruler goes the same way.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The halfway mark shows which numbered mark is closer.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The halfway mark shows which numbered mark is closer.

beats.say: Count the spaces from the start to that mark.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Count the spaces from the start to that mark.

beats.say: The start plus the length lands on that mark.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The start plus the length lands on that mark.
